meta.fallback: Hmm, I don't have an answer for that one. Try asking about my experience, my apps, my skills or how to reach me, or just email me at carlosanielrf@gmail.com.

topics.answer: Hi, I'm Carlos! I build iOS apps, and I'm based in Coimbra, Portugal. Ask me anything about my work, my apps or how I like to build things.
Thanks for stopping by, it was nice chatting! If you'd like to keep the conversation going, drop me a line at carlosanielrf@gmail.com.

Pretty much anything about my work: my job at Bosch, what I did before, Periplum (my own app), my tech stack, how I approach architecture and testing, my education, or how to get in touch. Just ask the way you would in person.

I'm an iOS developer, and I've been shipping apps to the App Store for 7 years. I started on a B2B marketplace that launched in 20 countries, then a Portuguese C2C marketplace, and for the last five years I've been at Bosch, working on the apps people use to control their home heating from their phone. In my own time I built Periplum, my own iOS app, on my own from the first commit to the store listing.

questions: How many years of experience do you have?
How long have you been an iOS developer?
topics.answer: About 7 years as an iOS developer, since January 2019. Before that I spent a few months doing web development, starting in September 2018.

questions: What do you do at the moment?
topics.answer: I'm an iOS developer at Bosch Thermotechnology in Aveiro, and I've been there since July 2021. I build and maintain the connected-heating apps for four Bosch brands.

questions: Which apps do you work on at Bosch?
What Bosch apps have you built?
Tell me about Vulcano Connect and IVT Anywhere
topics.answer: There are four: HomeCom Easy, MyBuderus, Vulcano Connect and IVT Anywhere. At heart they all do the same thing, letting people control their home heating from their phone, and they all ship from one shared iOS codebase.

questions: How do you handle four brands in one codebase?
Tell me about the shared codebase
topics.answer: It's all one iOS codebase for the four brands. The hard part, and the interesting one, is making one interface work for a whole catalogue of appliance types and generations, and for people of all ages across lots of countries and languages.

questions: How does the app talk to the appliance?
topics.answer: Yes. I work on the part where the app talks to the actual heating appliance, and it has to get that right every time. When that link fails, people feel it at home, so I give it the same care as anything on screen.

questions: Do you have machine learning experience?
topics.answer: A bit, yes. At Bosch I tested a Core ML model that runs on the device and spots faults in an appliance by looking at its heating and cooling data.

questions: Where did you work before Bosch?
topics.answer: Before Bosch I was at Appsconcept, at IPN in Coimbra. I joined as a web developer in September 2018, moved to iOS in January 2019, and stayed until July 2021.

questions: Tell me about Agriaffaires and Truckscorner
What apps did you build from scratch?
topics.answer: That was my big from-scratch project at Appsconcept: a B2B marketplace that launched in 20 countries as three apps, MachineryZone, Agriaffaires and Truckscorner. Three business models on one shared codebase, and all three held above 3.3★ in France, their main market.

questions: Tell me about the app rating improvement
Have you improved an app's rating?
topics.answer: CustoJusto is a Portuguese C2C marketplace that I maintained. I went through the reviews, fixed the problems people kept mentioning, and the App Store rating went up two stars, to 4.5★.

questions: Have you worked with React or Angular?
topics.answer: Yes, that's actually where I started. From 2018 to 2019 I worked on a big-data dashboard in React and Angular that built charts tailored to each client, and it taught me how much analytics shapes a product. I also worked on an on-site AR preview tool for a construction company.
A little. I worked on a preview tool for a construction company: you pointed the camera at physical markers on site and saw foundations and structures that hadn't been built yet.

questions: Tell me about your own app
Have you built an app alone?
topics.answer: Periplum is my own iOS app, and it's live on the App Store in Portugal, Spain, France and Italy. I did it all myself: design, architecture, code, release, even the store listing.

It's built with SwiftUI and SwiftData on iOS 18, with Swift 6 strict concurrency, and the domain logic lives in its own local Swift package. It has widgets for the Home Screen, Lock Screen and Control Center, App Intents so it works with Shortcuts and Siri, StoreKit 2 purchases with entitlement verification, 6 locales through String Catalogs, and Firebase for sign-in, analytics and crash reports.

questions: Can I see your apps on the App Store?
Where can I download your apps?
topics.answer: Sure, here's everything I've shipped or maintained. The Bosch apps and Periplum are what I'm working on now; CustoJusto and the B2B marketplace apps are from 2019 to 2021.

iOS: Swift, SwiftUI, UIKit, SwiftData, Swift Concurrency, RxSwift, WidgetKit, App Intents, StoreKit 2, MapKit, PDFKit, Core ML
Also: Kotlin Multiplatform, JavaScript, React, Angular
Architecture: MVVM, MVP, MVC, VIPER
Tooling: SPM, CocoaPods, Carthage, Swift Testing, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Travis CI, TestFlight
Other: REST APIs, Swagger, Firebase, String Catalogs, Zeplin, Confluence

Swift and SwiftUI are what I use every day, and I have plenty of UIKit experience too. Along the way I've also worked with RxSwift, SwiftData, WidgetKit, App Intents, MapKit, PDFKit, StoreKit 2, Core ML and Swift Concurrency, on both iPhone and iPad.
Yes, I use it in my day-to-day work, and Periplum runs on Swift 6 strict concurrency.

questions: Which programming languages do you know?
topics.answer: Mostly Swift. I also know Kotlin Multiplatform and JavaScript.

questions: How do you structure an app?
topics.answer: I've used MVVM, MVP, MVC and VIPER, and I pick whichever one actually helps the project. For dependencies I've worked with SPM, CocoaPods and Carthage. In Periplum I keep the domain logic in a local Swift package, separate from the UI.

questions: How do you test your apps?
topics.answer: Yes, I do. Periplum has 449 automated tests written with Swift Testing, and CI runs them on every push. At Bosch I test the REST endpoints against the product requirements every release, so if an API contract drifts, we catch it before customers do.
Yes. I work with REST API design and Swagger, and I check API contracts before a release, not after, so any drift gets caught before customers see it.

questions: Which CI tools do you use?
topics.answer: I've used GitHub Actions, Jenkins and Travis CI, with TestFlight for betas. I've taken apps all the way to release, App Store listing included.

Yes. I've worked with designers through Zeplin and documented things in Confluence, and I use Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics to see what's really happening in the app. Working on analytics dashboards early on showed me how much data shapes product decisions.
Quite a lot, yes. Periplum ships in 6 locales using String Catalogs, the Bosch apps are used across many countries and languages, and the B2B marketplace launched in 20 countries.
I have a Bachelor's degree in Multimedia from Instituto Superior Miguel Torga, which I did from 2015 to 2018.
Portuguese is my native language, and I speak English at a professional working level.
I live in Coimbra, Portugal.

I've shipped at scale: 20 countries, and four brands from one codebase. I've turned an app's reputation around, taking CustoJusto up two stars to 4.5★. And I can take an app from the first commit to the App Store on my own, like I did with Periplum. I also care about the parts users never see, like API contracts, tests and hardware integration.
Email is easiest: carlosanielrf@gmail.com. You can also find me on LinkedIn at linkedin.com/in/carlosaniel. Happy to chat!
It's github.com/Carlosanielrf, feel free to have a look around.
Of course. There's a PDF of my CV linked at the top of this page.
No, this isn't ChatGPT. A small model runs right here in your browser and matches your question to answers I wrote myself. There's no server or API behind it, so it can't make things up about me.

questions: Are you open to new opportunities?
Are you looking for a job?
Would you consider a new role?
topics.answer: Yes, I'm open to new opportunities. If you have a role in mind, I'd be glad to hear about it at carlosanielrf@gmail.com.
I prefer remote. Hybrid works too, if the office is within a reasonable distance of Coimbra.
I don't have kids.
I'm not married.

What do you do for fun?
What are your interests outside of work?
What do you do on weekends?
What do you like outside work?
topics.answer: Outside work I go to the gym and run, and I like eating out and going to the beach. Whenever I can, I go hiking on trails with my dog.
